question: An object is placed between the focus and the pole of a concave mirror, the image formed will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual, erect and enlarged**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is placed between the focus (F) and the pole (P) of a concave mirror, the image formed is virtual.
 
• The image is erect, meaning it is upright and not inverted.
 
• The image is enlarged, appearing larger than the object.
 
• This type of image is formed behind the mirror.
 
• The rays appear to diverge from a point behind the mirror, leading to the virtual image formation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Real Image**

 
 
• A real image is formed when light rays actually converge at a point.
 
• It is always inverted and can be projected onto a screen.
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror**
 
 
• A concave mirror is a mirror with a surface that curves inward like a bowl.
 
 
• **Convex Mirror**
 
 
• A convex mirror has a surface that curves outward.
 
• It always forms virtual, erect, and diminished images regardless of the object's position.
